To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the inclusive structure function of a large nucleus, $F_2^A,$ is expected to scale diffusively at large energies and small $x$ (i.e., for $Q^2 \ll Q^2_{\rm sat}$) and ii) diffractive scattering is expected to be suppressed in this regime.

the Pomeron loop corrections to the inclusive and diffractively produced cross sections are positive and that the diffusively scaled cross sections, defined as $Q^2 \sigma_{\rm tot} / \sigma_{\gamma^*p}^{\rm tot}$ versus $Q^2 / Q^2_{\rm sat},$ are universal, i.e. independent of $Q^ 2,$ in the kinematic region where they exist.

the diffractive cross-section of deep inelastic scattering is dominated by the exchange of a Pomeron loop, that the diffractively scattered partons are predominantly produced in pairs and that the Pomeron loop is responsible for diffusive scaling in the kinematical domain where the proton saturation momentum is exceeded.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the high-energy behavior of the cross-section for the inclusive and diffractively produced lepton-hadron deep inelastic scattering (DIS) process.
the high-energy behavior of the structure function $F_2,$ and with the high-energy limit of the diffractive structure function $F_{2D}.$
the study of the high-energy behavior of deep-inelastic processes, in the context both of inclusive and of diffractive scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at high energies, diffusive scaling is the most natural and robust scaling law in QCD, and that it is the most natural generalization of the BFKL approach, in particular, of the DGLAP approach.
, while the inclusive structure function $F_2$ at small $x$ and $Q^2$ is still well described by the DGLAP equations, at high enough $Q^2\gg Q_0^2$ the DGLAP approximation breaks down.

the QCD evolution equations for deep-inelastic scattering, including the BFKL and BK equations, are not sufficient to describe the full range of energy and $Q^2$ that can be explored at present and in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

diffusive scaling is the high-energy limit of inclusive and diffracted deep inelastic scattering, in which Pomeron loops dominate and the saturation momentum $Q_{sat}$ plays the role of the saturation scale.

the high-energy limit of inclusive deep inelastic scattering can be understood within a simple framework, where the leading contribution comes from a single Pomeron exchange, and the next-to-leading one comes from the exchange of two Pomerons.
the diffusive scaling law emerges as a consequence of the Pomeron loop effects, which are the dominant effects in the high energy limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

diffusive scaling, which is the result of a non-trivial interplay between the Pomeron loops and the BFKL evolution, can be used to constrain the Pomeron intercept, which is a fundamental parameter of the theory.
the Pomeron loops, which are expected to be important in the high-energy limit, are not negligible in the kinematical range currently probed at the LHC.
diffusive scaling, which is the high-energy limit of diffraction, should be experimentally observable in the very high-energy regime of the EIC.
